response.reason: The cited clause (Art. 26(2)(a) of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011) establishes that the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance is mandatory if omitting it could mislead consumers about the true origin of the food, especially if the labeling might otherwise suggest a different origin. The verdict turns on this requirement, stating that the origin is declared and there is no misleading omission. Therefore, the clause directly supports the legal basis for the verdict.
